title_he: הַמֵּת בַּעֲדֵנוּ בַּצְּלָב — הוּא אֲדֹנֵינוּ יֵשׁוּעַ

lines: כִּי הוּא נֶאֱמָן וְצַדִּיק, הוּא אָדוֹן חַנּוּן

review: The hymn is the promise of answered prayer: 1:1–3 is 1 John 5:14–15 with Num 23:19, 2:1–4 is John 14:13–14 with Rom 10:9, 3:1–4 is Ps 37:4 (וְהִתְעַנַּג עַל־יְהוָה) with Mal 3:10 (אֲרֻבּוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם) and Rev 3:20, and 4:1–4 is Isa 40:31 verbatim in its images.

Stanza 1 has three printed lines and stanzas 2–4 have four; the shape is 3/4/4/4 and the first stanza's short opening line is the whole thesis ('this is His word, this is His purpose'), so the payload keeps three lines and does not pad the stanza.

1:2 אִם־נֹאחֵז בּוֹ — the Arabic فَلَوْ تَمَسَّكْنَا بِهِ is a conditional whose apodosis the Arabic states loosely ('it would surely be ours'); the Hebrew uses the Niphal of אָחַז, the verb of Isa 27:5 and Job 27:6 for laying hold, and keeps the imperfect יִהְיֶה, so the line promises without asserting that the holding has already happened.

3:3 וִיעַשֵּׁר — the Arabic يُغْنِي حَيَاتَكَ is 'enriching your life'; the Hebrew uses the Hiphil of עָשַׁר, the verb of 1 Sam 2:7 (מַשְׁפִּיל אַף־מְרוֹמֵם), so the enrichment is God's own act and not a metaphor for contentment.

4:1–2 קֹוֵי יְהוָה יַחֲלִיפוּ / יַחֲלִיפוּ כֹחַ גָּדוֹל — the Arabic يُجَدِّدُونَ قُوَّةً is one clause; the Hebrew splits Isa 40:31's וְקֹוֵי יְהוָה יַחֲלִיפוּ כֹחַ across the two printed lines and repeats the verb, which is the only way to keep the stanza's two short lines at the printed length without adding a word the verse does not have.
